meta.title: Cloud computing
meta.subtitle: AWS vs. Azure vs. Google Cloud
meta.coverage_universe: Three hyperscalers; not the entire cloud market
meta.decision_use: Historical business and industry analysis; not a stock-price valuation

executive_view.headline: AWS leads on disclosed scale. Google Cloud grows faster. Azure needs a separate lens.
executive_view.summary: The comparison supports three distinct observations: AWS remains the larger of the two directly reported cloud segments, Google Cloud expanded faster and became profitable, and Azure’s growth is visible without a complete standalone profit history. None of those observations establishes market share or AI-specific returns.

panels.title: AWS: scale plus substantial segment profit
panels.text: AWS generated more revenue and operating profit than Google Cloud throughout this comparison. Revenue growth accelerated after 2023, while the operating margin fell in 2025 from its 2024 level. Scale did not eliminate investment or depreciation pressure.

panels.title: Google Cloud: faster growth, from a smaller base
panels.text: Google Cloud grew faster over the full period and moved from a reported operating loss to a substantial profit. Its business includes Workspace, and some shared AI research expense remains outside the segment; the margin is not a pure GCP or AI return measure.

panels.title: Azure: strong growth, incomplete segment economics
panels.text: Microsoft disclosed a revenue threshold for Azure in FY2025 and annual growth metrics. The reviewed reports do not provide a complete, exact five-year Azure revenue and operating-profit series. Intelligent Cloud and Microsoft Cloud would answer different questions.

map_cards.title: AWS | breadth and existing workload base
map_cards.text: Consumption-led infrastructure and platform services. Its demonstrated revenue and profit scale gives it resources to invest. The vulnerability is sustaining growth while capacity and depreciation costs rise; the accounts do not isolate AI profitability.

map_cards.title: Azure | enterprise software adjacency
map_cards.text: Cloud services sit alongside Microsoft’s enterprise software and developer offerings. That distribution is a plausible competitive advantage, not proof of customer conversion or market-share gains. Segment changes and limited standalone disclosure constrain margin comparisons.

map_cards.title: Google Cloud | GCP and Workspace
map_cards.text: GCP infrastructure and platform services combine with Workspace subscriptions. Faster reported growth and the move to profit are visible; how much came from share gains, market expansion, pricing or AI cannot be decomposed from these annual disclosures.

watches.title: Growth quality
watches.text: Track consumption growth, contract conversion and disclosed AI contributions separately. Aggregate revenue growth is an observed result; calling all of it AI demand would be an unsupported attribution.

watches.title: Capacity economics
watches.text: Read cash capex, finance leases, depreciation policies and margins together. Parent capex includes non-cloud uses and is not a denominator for an Azure, AWS or GCP return-on-investment calculation.

watches.title: Comparable disclosure
watches.text: Watch changes in Azure scope and Alphabet cost allocation. Obtain a consistent external market definition before calculating market share; growth relative to a peer does not identify where its customers came from.

methods.title: Two time bases, not one
methods.text: AWS and Google Cloud use years ending December 31. Microsoft uses fiscal years ending June 30. A Microsoft FY2025 figure covers July 2024–June 2025, not calendar 2025. No calendarization or time-shifted ranking is implied.

methods.title: Revenue is not market share
methods.text: AWS and Google Cloud have different product scopes; Google Cloud includes Workspace. Azure and other cloud services is neither Intelligent Cloud nor Microsoft Cloud. There is no complete market denominator here; no market-share percentage is calculated.

methods.title: Historical cost comparability
methods.text: Google Cloud CY2021–CY2022 operating results use the recast values in the 2023 annual filing; the overlapping 2023 values match the 2025 filing. Segment profit excludes some group costs. AWS useful-life changes also affect reported operating margins.

methods.title: Observed results versus explanations
methods.text: Revenue, cash expenditure and reported profit are historical actuals. Management’s explanations are labeled as such; competitive advantages are analytical assessments. No management capacity plan is counted as realized revenue, and no forecast is presented.

methods.title: Azure threshold and growth series
methods.text: The FY2025 Azure disclosure is greater than $75 billion, not exactly $75 billion. Growth rates are preserved as reported in each annual report; definitions and segment presentation evolved. No missing historical revenue or Azure margin is back-solved.

evidence.locator: CEO letter, financial performance
evidence.content: Microsoft says Azure annual revenue surpassed $75 billion. This is a lower bound, not an exact amount.

evidence.locator: Item 1, Business, AWS segment; Competition
evidence.content: AWS sells technology services including compute, storage, databases and analytics to enterprises, governments, start-ups and other customers. Competition includes infrastructure and cloud service providers.

evidence.locator: Note 15, segment information
evidence.content: Google Cloud includes Google Cloud Platform, Google Workspace and other enterprise services; revenue includes consumption and subscriptions.

evidence.locator: Business, Intelligent Cloud and Productivity and Business Processes; Metrics
evidence.content: Azure and other cloud services includes cloud and AI consumption services, GitHub cloud, Nuance Healthcare cloud and other services. Microsoft 365 is reported separately; Microsoft changed segment presentation for FY2025.

evidence.locator: Note 15, segment information
evidence.content: Alphabet simplified cost allocation in Q1 2023 and recast prior periods. Certain group-level costs are not assigned to operating segments.

evidence.locator: Item 7, segment results; Note 15
evidence.content: Alphabet-level activities primarily include shared AI research and development expenses. Google Cloud is therefore not a fully loaded standalone AI profit and loss statement.

evidence.locator: Item 7, revenues, Google Cloud
evidence.content: Management attributes the CY2025 revenue increase mainly to GCP growth in infrastructure and platform services, not exclusively to AI.

evidence.locator: Note 1, Property and Equipment
evidence.content: Server useful life increased from five to six years in 2024; a subset of servers and network equipment changed from six to five years in 2025. Reported margins therefore reflect accounting estimates as well as operations.

evidence.locator: MD&A, industry trends and opportunities; cash flows; Note 14, leases
evidence.content: Management describes increased investment in AI infrastructure. Cash property additions exclude non-cash finance-lease additions and are not Azure-only expenditure.
